question_7844865009: My most significant graph-theory work was my FlyWire connectome analysis project, where the problem was to infer latent neuronal types and class-dependent wiring patterns from neuronal connectivity graphs. I implemented Bayesian stochastic block models with class-dependent and spatially informed connectivity likelihoods, then applied them to FlyWire chemical-synapse networks by constructing thresholded adjacency matrices and evaluating cell-type recovery across brain regions. My specific contribution was the modeling and evaluation pipeline: representing connectome data as graphs, testing when spatial assumptions helped or failed, and extending the structural model with simulated neural activity. I also developed a burst-based Poisson spike-train simulator and incorporated co-firing-based functional connectivity into a joint structural–functional inference objective to study unresolved latent-block distinctions.
